# Neighbour-count selection for the k-th-NN attention distance on the validation set
# figure: knn_k_selection
# source: /home/paul/Code/Atoms_Carla/data/TFV6/val_data_alt
# Generated by figure_notes.py — do not edit; regenerate with the figure.

    BOTH SPLITS since 2026-09-03. Validation solid, test dotted. Validation-only, this figure read as though it contradicted the test-set figures; it does not, it is a different split, and k is selected on the validation curve alone.
    AUROC here is a single pooled AUROC over the FULL validation set INCLUDING Gaussian noise, per k, exactly as run_analysis.py selects k. It is one detector, not a mean over detectors, and it includes Gaussian noise, so it is NOT the criterion used for K in auroc_val_test_vs_K.
    Because the split holds exactly 200 frames of each perturbation and all of them are scored against the same 200 clean frames, a pooled AUROC is identically the unweighted mean of the per-perturbation AUROCs in the pool. Verified to machine precision for every detector. The two are not competing quantities; only the set of perturbations in the pool distinguishes the figures. Here the pool holds all four perturbations.
    'single' scores against the whole 5124-frame baseline. 'GMM' routes each sample to its nearest of the 8 components and scores within that component's pool only, falling back to the full baseline when the pool holds fewer than k frames.
    component sizes ascending: 96, 147, 158, 180, 453, 776, 1225, 2089
    k values exceeding the smallest component: 100, 250  (those k trigger the full-baseline fallback for that component's samples)
    components smaller than k = 100: 1  (of 8)
    components smaller than k = 250: 4  (of 8)

Routing, and how many samples the fallback actually touches
-----------------------------------------------------------
    Counting components exceeded understates the fallback: what matters is how many samples are ROUTED to a component too small for k, since those are scored against a reference set of a different size and therefore on a different scale, mixed into one ranking with the rest.
    baseline frames per component: 0 = 158, 1 = 2089, 2 = 96, 3 = 453, 4 = 147, 5 = 776, 6 = 180, 7 = 1225
    validation samples routed to each component: 0 = 134, 1 = 114, 2 = 172, 3 = 72, 4 = 70, 5 = 170, 6 = 56, 7 = 212
        component 0: 3.1% of the baseline, 13.4% of the validation samples
        component 1: 40.8% of the baseline, 11.4% of the validation samples
        component 2: 1.9% of the baseline, 17.2% of the validation samples
        component 3: 8.8% of the baseline, 7.2% of the validation samples
        component 4: 2.9% of the baseline, 7.0% of the validation samples
        component 5: 15.1% of the baseline, 17.0% of the validation samples
        component 6: 3.5% of the baseline, 5.6% of the validation samples
        component 7: 23.9% of the baseline, 21.2% of the validation samples
    validation samples falling back at k = 100: 172  (17.2%, from 1 component(s))
    validation samples falling back at k = 250: 432  (43.2%, from 4 component(s))
    Fallback rule, verified in run_analysis.py step 9b.3 (`if len(_pool) < _k: _pool = baseline_series`): the pool is replaced by the FULL baseline. It is not clamped and not padded, and DistanceComputer.compute_knn_distance raises rather than clamping, so the caller is the only place this is handled. Same rule as the Atari implementation.

Selection, and whether it transfers
-----------------------------------
    single: k chosen on validation: 1  (test AUROC there 0.5919)
    single: k that would have won on test: 1  (test AUROC 0.5919, cost of selecting on validation 0.0000)
    gmm: k chosen on validation: 50  (test AUROC there 0.5527)
    gmm: k that would have won on test: 100  (test AUROC 0.5676, cost of selecting on validation 0.0148)
    validation prefers: GMM at k = 50 (0.6159) over single at k = 1 (0.6055)
    test at those same two settings: GMM k = 50: 0.5527, single k = 1: 0.5919  (the selection reverses between the splits)

The two variants against each other, on validation
--------------------------------------------------
    difference at k = 1: 0.000525  (they should nearly coincide here, since the single nearest baseline frame is usually inside the sample's own component)
    k = 1: single 0.6055, GMM 0.6060  (GMM minus single +0.0005)
    k = 5: single 0.5904, GMM 0.6022  (GMM minus single +0.0118)
    k = 10: single 0.5854, GMM 0.6024  (GMM minus single +0.0170)
    k = 25: single 0.5719, GMM 0.6040  (GMM minus single +0.0321)
    k = 50: single 0.5638, GMM 0.6159  (GMM minus single +0.0522)
    k = 100: single 0.5559, GMM 0.5524  (GMM minus single -0.0035)
    k = 250: single 0.5553, GMM 0.5290  (GMM minus single -0.0263)
    selected GMM peak over its neighbours: k=25: 0.6040, k=50: 0.6159, k=100: 0.5524  (how isolated the selected point is)
    GMM best minus single best: 0.01043
